newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada-to-Chicago gas line files with U.S. FERC.
newsitem.headline: Canada-to-Chicago gas line files with U.S. FERC.

text.p: The group of Canadian energy firms aiming to build a natural gas pipeline to Chicago from northern Canada said on Tuesday it filed its application to build and operate the United States portion of the line.

Alliance Pipeline, a producer-backed pipeline that would carry 1.25 billion cubic feet of gas per day along the 3,000 km route, said it applied to the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for permission to build the system in the U.S. Midwest.

The consortium also said it would file with Canada's National Energy Board a "Notice of Intent" before the end of the year to inform the regulator that it would be submitting a similar application for the Canadian portion of the system in mid-1997.
Proponents of the C$3.6-billion project include 18 companies, including Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, Alberta Energy Co Ltd and IPL Energy Inc.
Its backers said the regulatory filings reinforced its commitment to shippers to meet the scheduled in-service date. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
